guard: `cotal up --no-manager` brings up the broker and, in auth mode, the delivery daemon, without starting a manager or writing its pidfile. A refresh under the flag refuses to keep or stop a live manager and tells the operator how to restart the stack broker-only.
why: The suite drives the shipped CLI on open and authenticated brokers and checks process records and startup reports.

Removing the broker-only branch in `ensureControlPlane` skips recording the manager omission and lets startup reach `ensureManager`. Delivery setup and the refusal for an already-live manager are unchanged.

mutations.name: drop the flag's effect in ensureControlPlane (ensureManager runs anyway)
mutations.expectRed: a --no-manager open refresh stays broker-only and exits 0
mutations.cell: a --no-manager open refresh stays broker-only and exits 0
mutations.note: The first broker-only refresh that reaches `ensureControlPlane` runs after the open mesh's manager has stopped. Falling through to `ensureManager` restores that manager, writes its pidfile, and prints the restored-manager line, so the open-refresh assertion fails before the later authenticated boot checks. The live-manager refusal runs before `ensureControlPlane` and is unaffected.
